subject: convergence with a piece wise regression model.

messages.author: 21b39e2b255e81ed
messages.subject: convergence with a piece wise regression model.
parts:
I am analyzing a longitudinal study, and would like to understand how much the effect of covariates is carried over the time. Therefore, I start with a simple regression when only use the t_i-1 to predict the outcome at t_i; 
y = a * x_t1 + e
and then use t_i-1 and t_i-2 to predict the t_i and see if the performance improves.
y = a *x_t1 + b * x_t2 + e

Still the above-mentioned models are not a time series model because covariates are independent. 
I thought to fit a model as following, in order to pass information between time points;  

but I have the convergence problem. 
y = e + c(a * x_t1 + d * x_t2)

This model converges when c is constant; but the problem raises when it becomes a variable in the model.

data {
  int<lower=0> Nobs; // number of subjects
  int<lower=0> Ngroup; // number of taxa
  int<lower=1> group_id[Nobs]; //indicator variable for each observation
  vector[Nobs] y; //body weight
  vector[Nobs] x_pt1; // abundance matrix
  vector[Nobs] x_pt2; // abundance matrix
}

parameters {
  vector[Ngroup] b; // slop for each group
  vector[Ngroup] etta; // intercept for each group
  vector[Ngroup] alpha_2;
  vector[Ngroup] alpha_1;
  vector<lower=0>[Ngroup] sigma; //error scale
}

model {
  for (i in 1:Nobs){
    y[i] ~ normal(etta[group_id[i]] + b[group_id[i]] * (alpha_2[group_id[i]] * x_pt2[i] + alpha_1[group_id[i]] * x_pt1[i]), sigma[group_id[i]]);
  }
}

messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Re: convergence with a piece wise regression model.
parts:
Hi,

This is a case of multiplicative non-identifability. As you have the model now, the product term does not have a solution, since you can multiply and divide either term by a constant and arrive at the same product. One solution is to put priors on your coefficients so they are constrained.  There is a section in the manual on this.

Matt

One solution is to put priors on your coefficients so they are constrained. There is a section in the manual on this.
>

The problematic priors chapter discusses the additive case and
I think also the multiplicative case for IRT. Something has
to define the scale.

The other problem is that with multiplicative non-identifiability
in the likelihood (even with a prior for weak identification),
you tend to get banana-shaped marginal posteriors in the non-identified
parameters which is very hard to sample because the covariance
varies around the banana.

> Matt
